column1: # Host normalization table for CDV GenBank records.
# `pattern` is matched case-insensitively as a substring of the /host qualifier.
# Order matters: the FIRST match wins, so specific patterns must sit above
# TWO kinds of ordering error, both fixed below. Both are silent.
#   1. GROUP ERROR — the record lands in the wrong discrete-trait state and
#      contributes a host transition that never happened.
#      (wild_felid) before `sea lion` (pinniped), so a pinniped entered the
#      tree as Panthera leo. The `sea lion` rule was unreachable.
#   2. SPECIES-NAME ERROR — the group is right but the canonical name is
#      another species. Harmless for the BEAST trait, wrong everywhere the
#      canonical name is shown: Auspice metadata, tables, figure legends.
#      Was: snow leopard -> Panthera pardus, mountain lion -> Panthera leo,
#      leopard cat -> Panthera pardus, maned wolf -> Canis lupus,
#      black-footed ferret -> Mustela putorius furo, arctic fox -> Vulpes sp.,
#      bobcat -> Lynx sp., sable -> Martes sp.
#   subspecies binomial  >  species binomial  >  specific common name
# A genus pattern (`vulpes`, `lynx`, `martes`, `mustela`) must sit BELOW every
# species in that genus, because real GenBank host strings carry both the
# binomial and the common name and the genus would otherwise win.
# host_group values used downstream as the BEAST discrete trait:
#   domestic_dog, wild_canid, wild_felid, mustelid, procyonid, pinniped,
#   ailurid, viverrid, ursid, primate, other, unknown
# Anything unmatched goes to needs_review.tsv for you to adjudicate.
# Vulpes species precede the genus and the bare noun.
# Common misspelling of Cerdocyon in GenBank submissions.
# NOTE: subspecies patterns MUST precede the species pattern, or the binomial
# match swallows them and you lose the Amur/Siberian distinction — which is the
# `snow leopard`, `leopard cat` and `amur leopard` MUST precede `leopard`.
# `sea lion` is the one that was changing the host GROUP.
# Mustela species precede `ferret` and the genus `mustela`.
# Neovison vison was reassigned to Neogale in 2021; both names are in GenBank.
# `sea lion` and `zalophus` are declared above, with the felids, so that they
# beat `lion`. Listing them here as well would be dead weight.
# Otariids (eared seals) before the bare `seal`, which would otherwise pull
# them into Phoca — a different family. Arctocephalus, Zalophus and Otaria are
# otariids; Phoca and Pusa are phocids.
# Non-carnivore hosts. CDV in these is notable but they are dead-end
# detections, not maintenance hosts -- grouped as 'other' and excluded from
# the discrete trait by the dta_states map.
